item.title: NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO & Board Director following input from US gov
item.dc:creator: Yimie Yong
item.description: "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," the company said in a statement.
item.content:encoded:
NASDAQ-listed chip maker NVIDIA announced on Monday that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the board, effective immediately.

“The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” the company said.

“In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the company said in a statement.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.”

According to the company, Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period,” said Jensen Huang.

“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work,” he added. 

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, NVIDIA said the board has formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation, the company said.

The board also reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The board said it has also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters, the company said.

NVIDIA said it is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

Earlier on Nov 12, NVIDIA‘s Board of Directors announced that Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board.

His resignation came after The New York Times reported that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with the company’s Vice President of Healthcare, Kimberly Powell. That prompted a last-minute board meeting, AFP news reported.

Huang reportedly acknowledged an affair with a woman accused of helping entities circumvent US export restrictions on high-performance chips to China, prompting the US chipmaker to launch an internal investigation.

item.title: AS Watson expands AI and robotics across retail supply chain
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: AS Watson is expanding AI and robotics across more than 55 distribution centers, reporting faster stock processing and doubled throughput at one facility.
item.content:encoded:
Hong Kong-based AS Watson Group is expanding the use of artificial intelligence, robotics and automation across more than 55 distribution centers, reporting faster stock processing and higher warehouse throughput as it modernizes a retail network spanning Asia and Europe.

The health and beauty retailer said on Monday that its supply-chain systems handled more than 3.7 billion items in 2025. The group operates more than 17,000 stores across 12 brands in 31 markets, including Watsons stores in China and other Asian markets.

At AS Watson’s distribution facility in Ede, the Netherlands, automation has doubled operational throughput while using the same workforce, according to the company. It also said an AI-supported process cut the time needed to compile inter-store stock transfers from six hours to 15 minutes.

The reported improvements come from a mix of automated guided vehicles, autonomous mobile robots, automated picking systems and AI-based demand forecasting. AS Watson is also using real-time inventory data and intelligent order routing to support its click-and-collect and delivery operations.

The company said it maintains nearly 99 percent on-shelf availability for fast-moving products. It did not disclose the period covered by that figure, the cost of the technology program or detailed methodology for the reported productivity improvements.

AS Watson is part of Hong Kong-listed CK Hutchison Holdings. The group said its broader technology-enabled retail platforms serve more than 6 billion shoppers annually, although that and the operational figures in Monday’s announcement are company-supplied and have not been independently audited.

The retailer also linked automation with changes in its warehouse workforce. Women account for nearly half of employees at its automated distribution centers, compared with about 30 percent at facilities without automation, according to AS Watson.

In Watsons China’s distribution-center network, the company said female representation in picking operations increased from 50 percent to 70 percent after automated systems were introduced. It attributed the change to reducing repetitive and physically demanding work, which it said made more warehouse roles accessible.

The deployment follows broader adoption of AI in retail planning and inventory management across Asia. In the Philippines, for example, Prince Retail expanded its use of AI-assisted supply-chain diagnostics this year to improve forecasting and product availability across its store network.

AS Watson said it will continue expanding its use of AI and automation to support demand without relying only on additional warehouse space or labor.

item.title: Maybank executes Malaysia’s first tokenized MGS transaction
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Malaysia's largest lender Maybank has successfully completed Malaysia’s first tokenized Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) transaction as part of a pilot with its insurance arm, Etiqa Life Insurance Berhad (Etiqa), marking a key milestone for Maybank’s initiative under Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub (DAIH).
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia’s largest lender Maybank has successfully completed Malaysia’s first tokenized Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) transaction as part of a pilot with its insurance arm, Etiqa Life Insurance Berhad (Etiqa), marking a key milestone for Maybank’s initiative under Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub (DAIH).

Under the pilot, Maybank and Etiqa executed a tokenized MGS trade, demonstrating how tokenized securities, tokenized deposits and custody processes can be composed into a programmable delivery-versus-payment (DvP) workflow spanning on-chain versus conventional infrastructure, the bank said in a statement on last Friday.

Maybank also provided custody services for the underlying physical cash and securities.

The pilot establishes a pathway towards more fluid settlements where cash, securities and collateral can be mobilized more seamlessly across counterparties.

When financial market infrastructure becomes increasingly digitized, such workflows could support more dynamic investments, funding and collateral activities.

These workflows also have the potential to automate transaction processes based on predefined conditions, and reduce settlement risks while improving liquidity, operational and capital efficiency.

This initiative underscores Maybank’s commitment to harnessing innovation and
delivering exceptional customer experiences, impacting society positively and benefiting the real economy, anchored on the Bank’s ROAR30 five-year strategy and purpose of Humanizing Financial Services.

“Tokenization is a natural expansion of financial services that we provide to our customers. It has the potential to fundamentally reshape how markets operate, enabling assets, cash and transactions to move more efficiently across financial markets,

“We see significant long- term opportunities in strengthening cross-border flows as ASEAN progresses towards deeper digital integration through initiatives such as the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA),” said Khairussaleh Ramli, President and Group Chief Executive Officer of Maybank.

“Our next phase will focus on scaling up our infrastructure to advance commercial applications, including tokenized bonds, deposits and other digital assets,

“Realizing this vision requires strong collaboration, and we welcome partnerships with technology players and industry participants,” he added.

Earlier this year, Maybank completed the first on-chain Malaysian Ringgit–Singapore Dollar foreign exchange conversion and cross-border payment for Yinson Holdings Berhad on the Bank’s permissioned blockchain.

Maybank also acted as Joint Lead Manager, Custodian and Primary Subscriber of Malaysia’s inaugural tokenized sukuk issuance by sovereign wealth fund Khazanah Nasional Berhad in collaboration with the Securities Commission in Malaysia.

Investing in digital innovation is part of Maybank’s ROAR30 planned commitment of MYR 10 billion ($2.43 billion) over the next five years in technology, data, and AI strategy to strengthen and scale long-term growth beyond 2030.

item.title: Vietnam’s $60M rare earth plant breaks ground, targets 10,000 tons a year
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Khanh An Industrial Park JSC kicked off the construction of a rare earth factory in Vietnam's coastal city of Hai Phong that will process rare earths into high-purity oxides.
item.content:encoded:
Khanh An Industrial Park JSC kicked off the construction of a rare earth factory in Vietnam’s coastal city of Hai Phong that will process rare earths into high-purity oxides.

In a statement on Monday, Hai Phong People’s Committee said Prime Minister Le Minh Hung attended a groundbreaking ceremony for the project and a port expansion. Singapore’s Ambassador to Vietnam, Rajpal Singh, and Japan’s Ambassador, Ito Naoki, attended, along with ministers and Hai Phong officials.

The factory has an investment of VND1,580 billion ($60 million). It covers 14 hectares in the Xuan Cau Industrial and Non-Tariff Zone in Cat Hai Special Zone.

The plant will use five hydrometallurgical separation lines with a total capacity of 10,000 tons a year. It will produce individual rare earth oxides with purity above 99 percent for use in electronics, semiconductors, new energy, and high-tech industries.

The factory aims to supply materials for high-performance permanent magnets, electronics, components, energy products, optics, and catalysts. The project can help diversify Vietnam’s industrial structure. Commercial operation is set to begin from the fourth quarter of 2028.

The ceremony also started berths 9 to 12 at the Lach Huyen port. The project has an investment of VND24,845 billion, ($945 million). The port project covers about 146.2 hectares and will add four container berths with a combined length of 1,800 meters. It can handle ships of 12,000-18,000 TEUs, doubling the throughput of the Lach Huyen deep-water port cluster.

Vietnam proposes 99% purity standard for rare earth exports

item.title: Singapore-based semiconductor company MetaOptics secures $25M from GEM Fund
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: MetaOptics, a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics firm providing glass-based metalens solutions, has secured S$32 million ($25 million) from GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd., a Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by New York-based Global Emerging Markets (GEM).
item.content:encoded:
MetaOptics, a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics firm providing glass-based metalens solutions, has secured S$32 million ($25 million) from GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd., a Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by New York-based Global Emerging Markets (GEM).

In a statement on Monday, MetaOptics said it signed a share subscription facility for the move on November 20. The agreement is subject to approval of its shareholders.

The investment is a three-year committed facility that lets the company decide the timing of each drawdown. This gives MetaOptics flexible access to growth capital in line with its capital needs and market conditions.

MetaOptics plans to use net proceeds from drawdowns for working capital, including general corporate expenses and day-to-day operations. It also plans to establish a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States to produce metalenses for co-packaged optics and color imaging applications. MetaOptics does not provide further details for the move.

Mr Thng Chong Kim, Executive Chairman of MetaOptics, said: “This Share Subscription Facility gives us a reliable, flexible source of capital for our day-to-day operations and to support the growth of our existing business by establishing a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States, on terms that put MetaOptics in control of the timing and size of each drawdown.”

Singapore’s MetaOptics secures up to $10M US investment facility

item.title: AI reshapes Singapore job market as employers prioritize skills, productivity in 2027 – survey
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is set to reshape Singapore's employment landscape in 2027, with companies placing greater emphasis on AI literacy, specialized technical expertise and workforce reskilling as automation changes job roles and skills requirements, recruitment firm Robert Walters said on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is set to reshape Singapore’s employment landscape in 2027, with companies placing greater emphasis on AI literacy, specialized technical expertise and workforce reskilling as automation changes job roles and skills requirements, recruitment firm Robert Walters said on Monday.

As AI adoption accelerates across organizations, some existing roles are expected to shrink or undergo significant changes, while demand grows for capabilities in AI implementation, data, cybersecurity, cloud computing and digital transformation, the firm said in its 2027 Salary Survey.

Robert Walters said employers would increasingly shift towards skills-based hiring, prioritizing demonstrated capabilities and practical experience over academic qualifications, job titles and conventional career paths.

Talent with AI literacy, including the ability to apply AI within their respective functions responsibly, will be particularly valued.

The growing skills gap is already prompting professionals to upgrade their capabilities, with 60 percent of those surveyed acknowledging a mismatch between their current skill sets and employers’ requirements.

Meanwhile, 54 percent are actively learning AI-specific skills, while another 25 percent are focusing on strengthening soft skills such as leadership, relationship building and judgement.

The shift comes as 78 percent of businesses expect up to half of their workforce to require reskilling due to AI advancements, based on Robert Walters’ 2026 research.

Robert Walters Singapore country manager Kirsty Poltock said companies were unlikely to return to broad-based salary inflation or indiscriminate hiring in 2027, instead directing investment towards critical skills while placing greater emphasis on productivity and workforce transformation.

The recruitment firm expects demand to remain strong for cybersecurity specialists, data and AI engineers, cloud engineers, as well as fintech, quantitative, risk and compliance professionals in financial services.

Beyond technical specialists, professionals who can translate technology into business outcomes, including transformation leaders, change managers and commercially minded technology talent, are also expected to be sought after.

However, employers face challenges in securing suitable candidates, with 75 percent citing a lack of quality applicants with the right skills and experience as a key recruitment obstacle. Another 58% pointed to high salary and benefit expectations.

Despite the demand for skilled talent, overall salary increases are expected to remain moderate in 2027. While 96 percent of companies surveyed intend to raise salaries, 65 percent plan to offer existing employees increments of at least 3 percent.

The survey also highlighted a gap between employers’ salary budgets and jobseekers’ expectations. While 49 percent of employers intend to offer new hires salary increases of at least 6 percent, 75 percent of professionals looking to change jobs expect increments exceeding 10 percent.

Professionals with scarce expertise in AI, data, cybersecurity, cloud and specialized financial services are likely to command higher salary increases, particularly those able to demonstrate measurable business impact.

Robert Walters also found that 78% of professionals are considering a job change in 2027, although only 48% are confident about securing new opportunities.

The survey, which gathered responses from 579 professionals and companies in Singapore in September 2026, also found that employers are increasingly looking beyond salary to retain talent, with job security, work-life balance and flexible working arrangements among professionals’ key considerations.

item.title: CIMIC’s Leighton Asia to acquire Malaysia’s LWE, expanding cleanroom capabilities
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Leighton Asia, under Australia-based CIMIC Group, will acquire Malaysian mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services company LWE and its cleanroom business CLIN.
item.content:encoded:
Leighton Asia, under Australia-based CIMIC Group, will acquire Malaysian mechanical, electrical, and plumbing services company LWE and its cleanroom business CLIN.

In a statement on Monday, HOCHTIEF, the parent firm of CIMIC, said the deal can strengthen Leighton Asia’s end-to-end capabilities in advanced technology. The company did not provide any details about finance or timeline.

The acquisition will enhance Leighton Asia’s offering for clients in high-growth sectors including semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, data centers, renewable energy, and industrial development. It will also add in-house MEP capability and established cleanroom fabrication capacity in Penang, Malaysia.

ACS Group and HOCHTIEF CEO and CIMIC Group Executive Chairman Juan Santamaría said “The acquisition of LWE and CLIN is aligned with our strategy to expand our capabilities in advanced technology and provide clients with more integrated, end-to-end solutions.”

“LWE and CLIN bring specialist expertise, established client relationships and more than four decades of experience. Combined with Leighton Asia’s regional presence and project delivery capability, this positions us to capture new opportunities in advanced technology and cleanroom markets across Asia, Australia and Europe,” the executive added.

Leighton Asia Managing Director Jan Torka said “LWE’s MEP expertise and CLIN’s cleanroom capabilities are a strong complement to our business. Cleanrooms are a critical component of advanced technology, semiconductor and pharmaceutical projects, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our position in these growing sectors.”

item.title: Votee AI partners AI Singapore to explore AI research for Southeast Asian languages
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Votee AI and AI Singapore (AISG) have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore research and development on large language models for Southeast Asian languages, with initial focus areas to be jointly prioritized.
item.content:encoded:
Votee AI and AI Singapore (AISG) have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore research and development on large language models for Southeast Asian languages, with initial focus areas to be jointly prioritized.

Under the MoU, the organizations intend to explore joint research, the exchange of technical know-how, shared evaluation benchmarks and co-authored publications, the duo said in a statement on last Friday.

The work is at an exploratory stage, with initial language priorities to be jointly discussed.

It is noted that more than 600 million people live in Southeast Asia, while many languages in the region remain underserved by global AI models.

The proposed work will explore models built with regional data and evaluated against regional benchmarks.

Votee AI aims to bring what it has learned building Cantonese language AI to other underserved languages.

Its engineering team includes developers based in Ho Chi Minh City, and the company plans to draw on them as the work extends to Southeast Asian languages.

“Asia Pacific is one of the fastest-growing markets for generative AI, yet language competency in low-resource languages remains a barrier to broader adoption. Through our MoU with AI Singapore, we look forward to exploring regional language-model research that can help bridge this divide and support AI adoption by governments and enterprises,

“Our experience developing Cantonese language AI and supporting its adoption gives us a strong foundation to contribute to this work with like-minded institutions such as AI Singapore,” said Pak-Sun Ting, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Votee AI.

Leslie Teo, Senior Director of AI Products, AI Singapore said that advancing AI for Southeast Asia requires collaboration across the ecosystem.

He said the exploration of joint research and shared evaluation benchmarks can raise the quality and reliability of language models for the region.

Jacky Chan, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Votee AI, also said the firm’s approach is consistent: rigorous benchmarks first, open research where possible, and models institutions can own and run on their own infrastructure.

“We co-authored HKCanto-Eval (CoNLL 2025) for Cantonese. We want Southeast Asian languages to have the same scientific foundation,” he added.

item.title: China’s MegaRobo raises nearly $200M for AI lab automation
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: China's MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200 million to expand AI-connected laboratory automation and physical-world intelligence systems.
item.content:encoded:
China-based MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200 million in a financing round to expand artificial intelligence systems that connect models and software with laboratory instruments, robotics and other physical equipment.

Oman Investment Authority, the sovereign wealth fund of Oman, joined the round, while existing investors Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures continued their backing. CMB International also participated as a new investor, according to MegaRobo’s November 18 announcement.

The company did not identify a lead investor, disclose a valuation or assign a formal stage to the round. It said it has raised approximately $600 million across multiple financing rounds, including a nearly $300 million Series C co-led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Asia Investment Capital and Granite Asia.

MegaRobo said the new capital will support core technology development, international expansion of its AI-for-science business and infrastructure that allows AI systems to operate across complex physical environments.

The company develops what it calls the One Intelligence Stack, which combines models and agents, data, workflows, scientific instruments and automation in one system. In laboratory use, the architecture is intended to let software design experiments, send instructions to robotic equipment, capture results and use the resulting data to guide subsequent work.

The platform is organized around a cycle of designing, executing, observing and learning from physical experiments. MegaRobo presents science as the first application because laboratory work requires software to move beyond analyzing digital information and interact directly with instruments, samples and changing experimental conditions.

The financing has direct regional relevance because MegaRobo is headquartered in China and plans to expand its operations across Asia as well as North America, Europe and the Middle East. Its systems also address pharmaceutical research and advanced manufacturing, including workflows in semiconductors and display production.

MegaRobo has delivered scientific-intelligence infrastructure to more than 500 pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology businesses, contract research organizations and research institutions. The company’s automated laboratory service has worked with more than 200 customers. Those operating figures originate from the company and have not been independently audited.

MegaRobo was founded in 2016. Earlier investors include WuXi AppTec and Bosch Ventures, while Pavilion Capital, part of Temasek’s Seviora Group, participated in the company’s previous Series C financing.

The company said it will use its technology beyond life sciences in physical systems that require AI to interact with instruments, machines, materials and production processes. It did not provide a deployment timetable, new customer commitments or a geographic breakdown for the expansion funded by the new round.

MEGAROBO Unveils High-Content Cell Imaging System for Advanced Multidimensional Biological Analysis

item.title: Vietnam-France-Korea consortium wins $423M design contract for Vietnam’s $67B high-speed railway
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: A consortium of firms from Vietnam, South Korea, and France has won a feasibility study and basic design contract for Vietnam's North-South high-speed railway, worth KRW560 billion ($423 million), South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said.
item.content:encoded:
A consortium of firms from Vietnam, South Korea, and France has won a feasibility study and basic design contract for Vietnam’s North-South high-speed railway, worth KRW560 billion ($423 million), South Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said.

In a statement on Sunday, the ministry said the contract was awarded on November 21. The consortium includes Korea Rail Network Authority (KNR), Samboo Engineering, and Yooshin Engineering from South Korea; France’s SYSTRA; and Vietnam’s Transport Engineering Design Incorporated (TEDI). The ministry said more than 40 rail design firms competed for the work.

The consortium will carry out the study and design over 30 months, from November 2026 to May 2029. The feasibility study is scheduled for 18 months and the basic design for 12 months.

The ministry emphasized the award as the largest overseas rail planning and design contract for South Korea. It credited the government’s support, including two summits between the leaders of Korea and Vietnam, in August 2025 and April 2026, and ministerial delegations in June and July 2026. A presidential letter was also delivered, the ministry added.

The full project would build a double-track high-speed line of about 1,541 kilometers from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, designed for speeds of 350 kilometers per hour. It would have four sections: Hanoi to Vinh (281 kilometers), Vinh to Da Nang (420 kilometers), Da Nang to Nha Trang (480 kilometers) and Nha Trang to Ho Chi Minh City (360 kilometers).

The ministry said construction is due to start in 2029 and the line to open in 2035. The total project cost is $67.3 billion.
